get.summary: GET /auth/redirect — Unified OAuth callback for BOTH providers.
get.description:
The deployed Google + GitHub OAuth apps share a single redirect URI
(`https://app.litegen.ai/api/auth/redirect`, served to the backend as
`/auth/redirect` once nginx strips `/api`). We disambiguate the provider via
the short-lived `litegen_oauth_provider` cookie set at `*_start`, then
dispatch to the matching core callback fn.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1–255 visible ASCII characters. The same key and the same request within 24 hours replay the first response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and bill nothing; the same key with a different request is a 409. A request refused before any vendor was called does not spend the key.

parameters.name: X-Litegen-Keep-Outputs
parameters.description: `false` keeps nothing for this request: no copy of the output is stored anywhere, and the answer carries the image itself or the vendor's own link (docs/storage-access.md). A request can keep less than its app does, never more; any other value is a 400 `invalid_keep_outputs_header`.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: RFC 7240. `respond-async` answers 202 as soon as the vendor has the job; `wait=N` waits up to N seconds (at most the vendor timeout) and answers 202 if the job is still running then. Honoured only for a model whose vendor runs jobs, a request that keeps its output and isn't an edit litegen finishes itself; otherwise the call is synchronous (`Preference-Applied` absent). See docs/async-images.md.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing ran and nothing was billed. Absent otherwise.

X-Litegen-Cache.description: What the cache did: `hit` (answered from it), `miss` (looked up, not found) or `bypass` (off for this model, or the request sent `Cache-Control: no-cache`). See docs/gateway-settings.md.

X-Litegen-Dropped-Params.description: Comma-separated names of params this request sent that the model does not support, dropped instead of refused because `strict` was false. Absent when nothing was dropped.

202.description: The vendor has the job and litegen delivers its image later (`Prefer: respond-async`, or a `wait` it outlasted): poll `GET /v1/generations/{id}` or wait for the key's webhook.

409.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_request_in_progress`: a request with this key is still running (`Retry-After` is set).

410.description: `model_retired`: the model is past its retirement; `replaced_by` names its successor

422.description: `region_too_small`: an edit region smaller than the vendor takes. A reference that names a generation litegen can't use (`reference_images`: unreadable, too large, a format the model doesn't take).

504.description: `vendor_timeout`: the vendor did not answer in time. Never re-sent, since the vendor may still run and bill the job; `vendor_job_id` names it when the vendor had accepted one. When that job can still be delivered, `generation_id` names the generation it goes to and `status` is `processing`.

post.summary:
POST /v1/images/segmentations — Masks for what point, box or text prompts
select in an image, answered at once.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1–255 visible ASCII characters. The same key and the same request within 24 hours replay the first response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and bill nothing; the same key with a different request is a 409. A request refused before any vendor was called does not spend the key.

200.description: What the prompts selected: one mask per object, best first, billed once per request at the row's price

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing ran and nothing was billed. Absent otherwise.

400.description: Refused before anything is billed. `param_required`: no prompts, or an empty text prompt. `capability_unsupported`: a prompt type the model does not take (its `segmentation_prompts`). `param_out_of_range`: more prompts than the model takes, more than one text prompt, a point label other than 0 or 1, or a box with no area. `param_conflict`: a text prompt mixed with point or box prompts, or only label-0 points. `prompt_out_of_bounds`: a point or box outside the image. `image_unreadable`: not base64 of a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF. `model_task_mismatch`: not a segmentation model. `model_media_type_mismatch`: not an image model.

402.description: `quota_exceeded` / `budget_exceeded`: the key's quota or a budget it counts against is spent.

409.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_request_in_progress`: a request with this key is still running (`Retry-After` is set).

410.description: `model_retired`: the model is past its retirement; `replaced_by` names its successor

429.description: `rate_limit_exceeded`: the key's requests per minute (`Retry-After` is set); or the vendor's own rate limit, retryable.

503.description: litegen is at capacity, or the app's bucket can't be reached; retry shortly.

504.description: `vendor_timeout`: the vendor did not answer in time. Never re-sent.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1–255 visible ASCII characters. The same key and the same request within 24 hours replay the first response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and bill nothing; the same key with a different request is a 409. A request refused before any vendor was called does not spend the key.

parameters.name: X-Litegen-Keep-Outputs
parameters.description: `false` keeps nothing for this request: no copy of the output is stored anywhere, and the answer carries the image itself or the vendor's own link (docs/storage-access.md). A request can keep less than its app does, never more; any other value is a 400 `invalid_keep_outputs_header`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing ran and nothing was billed. Absent otherwise.

X-Litegen-Dropped-Params.description: Comma-separated names of params this request sent that the model does not support, dropped instead of refused because `strict` was false. Absent when nothing was dropped.

400.description: Bad request: a request that fails validation (`param_*`, with `param`), or one that keeps nothing (`X-Litegen-Keep-Outputs: false`) yet asks litegen for something it makes from a file it keeps: a container it converts (`format_needs_keeping`) or an output option it applies (`option_needs_keeping`, naming the option in `param`, e.g. `output_packages`, `ktx2_textures`, `dae_morphs`, `usdz_root`, `usd_clips`)

409.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_request_in_progress`: a request with this key is still running (`Retry-After` is set).

410.description: `model_retired`: the model is past its retirement; `replaced_by` names its successor

422.description: A `source_model` litegen can't use (unreadable, too large, too many triangles, no skin to animate), or the vendor's free preflight refused it (its own code).

500.description: `generation_record_failed`: the vendor accepted the job but litegen could not record it, so it has no id to poll; `vendor_job_id` names the vendor's job. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` gets this answer, not a second job.

504.description: `vendor_timeout`: the vendor did not answer in time. Never re-sent, since the vendor may still run and bill the job; `vendor_job_id` names it when the vendor had accepted one.

post.summary: POST /v1/utils/models3d/convert — Convert a mesh between containers without generating anything.
post.description:
The body is the raw file. The response is the converted file, with the
target's `Content-Type`. Whatever the target container can hold survives
(materials, textures, skins, animation); what it cannot is dropped and
named in `X-Litegen-Conversion-Losses`. WebP and KTX2 (Basis Universal)
textures are re-encoded as PNG, as generations deliver them, so no
container drops them and, by default, no glTF requires
`EXT_texture_webp` or `KHR_texture_basisu` (`ktx2_textures=keep` leaves a
KTX2 in a glb or gltf, which then requires `KHR_texture_basisu`). By
default the output is one file: OBJ carries its materials as vertex
colours, and Collada, USDA and USDC leave textures out (named as losses).
`package=zip` answers with a zip of the file and its sidecars instead,
which keeps them. A USD file (`.usda`, `.usdc`, or a `.usd` holding either)
is read with `from=usda` or `from=usdc`, whichever encoding it is in.

Live: `curl --data-binary @fox.glb "https://app.litegen.ai/api/v1/utils/models3d/convert?from=glb&to=obj" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -o fox.obj`

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Container the request body is in. Must be one of `GET /v1/utils/models3d/formats`. `usda` and `usdc` each read either USD encoding, text or a binary crate (`.usdc`, or a `.usd` holding either).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Container to convert to. Must be one of `GET /v1/utils/models3d/formats`.

parameters.name: units
parameters.description: Only when `to` is `stl`, `obj` or `ply`, which carry no units: the unit the written numbers are in, `m` (the default), `cm`, `mm`, `in` or `ft`. Slicers read STL as millimetres.

parameters.name: up
parameters.description: Only when `to` is `stl`, `obj` or `ply`: the written up axis, `y` (the default, glTF's) or `z` (slicers, CAD, Blender), turning +Y up to +Z up and the front (+Z) to -Y.

parameters.name: from_units
parameters.description: Only when `from` is `stl`, `obj` or `ply`: the unit the body's numbers are in, as `units`. Default `m`.

parameters.name: from_up
parameters.description: Only when `from` is `stl`, `obj` or `ply`: the body's up axis, `y` (the default) or `z`.

parameters.name: fbx_color_space
parameters.description: Only when `from` or `to` is `fbx`: how FBX material and light colours are stored, at that end. `srgb` (the default; three.js reads them so) or `linear` (Blender, ufbx and assimp read both so, and Unity and Unreal material colours). Vertex colours are sRGB either way.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: `file` (the default) answers with the converted file alone; `zip` answers with a zip (`application/zip`, `model.<to>.zip`) of the file and the sidecars it references (an OBJ's `.mtl` and `textures/`, Collada's, USDA's and USDC's `textures/`, a `.gltf`'s `.bin` and images), at the paths it names them by, the file first. Unzipped, the folder opens as it is: an OBJ keeps its materials, Collada, USDA and USDC keep their textures, and the losses header is judged against the package. A single-file container (glb, fbx, stl, ply, 3mf, usdz) zips to one entry, the `file` answer byte for byte.

parameters.name: ktx2_textures
parameters.description: `png` (the default) re-encodes every KTX2 (Basis Universal) texture as PNG, as WebP is, so no container drops it and no glTF requires `KHR_texture_basisu`: ETC1S, UASTC and uncompressed RGBA8 KTX2 files decode, and the PNG holds the values the KTX2 stores, with no colour conversion. A KTX2 that cannot be decoded, or that would pass the 64 MiB texture budget, is left out and named as an `image_formats` loss. `keep` leaves the KTX2 as it is, byte for byte, when `to` is `glb` or `gltf`, referenced through `KHR_texture_basisu`, which the file then requires, so a reader with no KTX2 support may refuse it: it suits viewers that upload KTX2 to the GPU (three.js with KTX2Loader, Babylon.js, Godot). Every other `to` gets PNG whichever you choose.

schema.description:
What the converter does with a KTX2 (Basis Universal) texture
(`ktx2_textures`).

parameters.name: fbx_light_units
parameters.description: Only when `from` or `to` is `fbx`: the units FBX light strengths are stored in, at that end. `photometric` (the default) is the scene's own, glTF's: `Intensity` is 100 × the candela (point and spot lights) or lux (directional lights), which three.js's FBXLoader and ufbx read back. `blender` stores 100 × the `energy` Blender's own glTF importer gives the same scene's glTF light (a point or spot light's candela × 4π / 683 W, a directional light's lux / 683 W/m²), so the light opens in Blender as bright as the glTF does, and reads a light Blender wrote as the glTF light whose Blender glTF import gives that `energy`. Colour, cones and range are the same either way. The option applies at whichever end is fbx, so `from=fbx&to=fbx` with `blender` reads Blender's units and writes them back, a no-op: to move a Blender file to `photometric`, convert twice (fbx to glb with `blender`, then glb to fbx).

parameters.name: usd_light_units
parameters.description: Only when `from` or `to` is `usdz`, `usda` or `usdc`: the units USD light strengths are stored in, at that end. `photometric` (the default) is UsdLux's own, by the schema: a point or spot light is a normalised `SphereLight` of 4 × the candela, a directional light a normalised `DistantLight` of the lux (Storm, usdview's renderer, agrees on the sun and draws such a sphere 4× brighter). `blender` writes the UsdLux values Blender's USD exporter writes for the `energy` Blender's own glTF importer gives the same scene's glTF light (a point or spot light's candela × 4π / 683 W, a directional light's lux / 683 W/m²), so the light opens in Blender as bright as the glTF does, and reads a light prim without litegen's `customData` (every one Blender wrote) as the glTF light whose Blender glTF import gives that `energy`. A file litegen wrote also carries its exact strengths in `customData`, which litegen reads in preference to the UsdLux values under either choice. The option applies at whichever end is usdz, usda or usdc: `from=usdz&to=usdz` with `blender` keeps the strengths of a file in Blender's units, and rewrites those of a file litegen wrote in Blender's units, its `customData` keeping the exact values. To move a Blender file to `photometric`, convert twice (usdz to glb with `blender`, then glb to usdz).

parameters.name: dae_morphs
parameters.description: Only when `to` is `dae`: how Collada's morph targets (blend shapes) are written. `bake` (the default) applies the targets at each node's weights and drops their weight animation, which every Collada reader opens. `keep` writes them as `<morph>` controllers with their weight animation, which SceneKit (and so Xcode) and Godot read, while three.js's ColladaLoader and assimp refuse the whole file, so choose it only for a reader that opens controllers.

parameters.name: usdz_root
parameters.description: Only when `to` is `usdz`: what the package's root layer, its first entry, is. `usda` (the default) is USDA text, which `usdchecker --arkit` accepts (the rule demanding a crate was removed in OpenUSD 24.03) and which `<model-viewer>` hands to AR Quick Look as it is. `usdc` is the binary crate, as Apple's own packagers write it: the package is `model.usdc` and its textures, every entry stored and 64-byte aligned either way. The two read back as one scene.

parameters.name: usd_clips
parameters.description: Only when `to` is `usda`, `usdc` or `usdz`: which animation clips the USD file holds. `all` keeps every clip as an alternative, a variant set `Animation` on the default prim with one variant per clip, the first selected, so a reader that composes variants can switch between them and one that does not plays the first. Every clip's skeletal and blend-shape animation is kept; rigid (node) motion is the first clip's only, the other clips' is named in the losses, and a scene whose clips are all rigid writes as `first`. `first` keeps the first clip alone. The default is `all` for `usda` and `usdc`, `first` for `usdz` until AR Quick Look's behaviour with variants is checked on a device.

schema.description:
A mesh file as raw bytes, for the spec only: the handler reads the `Body`
directly. Without this, `Vec<u8>` documents as an array of integers and the
SDK generators type the upload as `number[]`.

200.description: The converted file, with the target container's Content-Type (e.g. model/obj); with `package=zip`, a zip of it and its sidecars (`application/zip`)

X-Litegen-Conversion-Losses.description: Comma-separated kinds of content in the input that the target container could not hold, in alphabetical order and deduplicated: animation, skins, morph_targets, normals, uvs, vertex_colors, textures, image_formats, materials, alpha, hierarchy, meshes, texture_sampling, texture_transforms, geometry, lights, cameras, points, lines. Judged from what the input actually contains: a mesh with no normals, materials or UVs loses nothing to STL, while one that has them names them. `points` and `lines` name point and line primitives (a point cloud, a wireframe) in a container that has none: STL, 3MF and FBX hold neither, Collada holds no points, and PLY holds points only in a file with no faces or edges. Absent when nothing was lost.

X-Litegen-Conversion-Warnings.description: What reading the input itself dropped or approximated, in prose, joined by `; `: a material library or texture the upload could not include, a glTF extension litegen does not carry (material variants, animation pointers, …), cubic and NURBS curves, a Gaussian splat's extra attributes, an FBX animation layer. Non-ASCII characters are replaced by `?`. Absent when the reader had nothing to say.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1–255 visible ASCII characters. The same key and the same request within 24 hours replay the first response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and bill nothing; the same key with a different request is a 409. A request refused before any vendor was called does not spend the key.

parameters.name: X-Litegen-Keep-Outputs
parameters.description: `false` keeps nothing for this request: no copy of the output is stored anywhere, and the answer carries the image itself or the vendor's own link (docs/storage-access.md). A request can keep less than its app does, never more; any other value is a 400 `invalid_keep_outputs_header`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing ran and nothing was billed. Absent otherwise.

X-Litegen-Dropped-Params.description: Comma-separated names of params this request sent that the model does not support, dropped instead of refused because `strict` was false. Absent when nothing was dropped.

409.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_request_in_progress`: a request with this key is still running (`Retry-After` is set).

410.description: `model_retired`: the model is past its retirement; `replaced_by` names its successor

422.description: A `source_video` or reference generation litegen can't use: unreadable, too large, or a format the model doesn't take.

500.description: `generation_record_failed`: the vendor accepted the job but litegen could not record it, so it has no id to poll; `vendor_job_id` names the vendor's job. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` gets this answer, not a second job.

504.description: `vendor_timeout`: the vendor did not answer in time. Never re-sent, since the vendor may still run and bill the job; `vendor_job_id` names it when the vendor had accepted one.

`storage_access.signed_url_ttl_seconds`.

vendor_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one vendor call may take, 5 to 3600. Overrides `server.vendor_timeout_secs`.

GatewaySettingsView.description:
Response for `GET /v1/admin/settings`: the stored overrides plus the
values in effect.

cache_entries.description: Answers the cache holds now (on this replica).

effective_cache.description: The cache in force: these settings, else `cache` in `litegen.yaml`.

effective_retries.description: Retries in force: these settings, else `retries` in `litegen.yaml`.

effective_storage_access.description:
Who may open stored outputs for an app with no settings of its own:
these settings, else `storage_access` in `litegen.yaml`.

effective_vendor_timeout_seconds.description: The vendor call timeout in force, in seconds.

Generation.description: A DB-backed generation row (video or image, currently used for video).

app_id.description: Owning application. None for pre-tenancy / untenanted rows.

files_deleted_at.description:
When litegen deleted this generation's kept files: after its app's
`retention_days`, or on request. The record stays. Absent while they
are kept.

key_id.description: API key that submitted this generation; None when master key was used.

org_id.description: Owning tenant (organization). None for pre-tenancy / untenanted rows.

provider_job_id.description: Provider-assigned job ID used for polling.

GenerationAsset.description:
One stored file of a generation of any kind, as
`GET /v1/generations/{id}/assets` lists it. litegen keeps every result for
at least 7 days; `GET /v1/generations/{id}/assets/{index}` streams it with
a litegen key alone, whatever the vendor's own URL did.

duration_s.description: Videos: length in seconds, when known.

expires_at.description:
When a signed link stops working (`docs/storage-access.md`); read the
generation again for a fresh one. Absent on every other URL.

format.description: Lowercase container or image format, without a dot.

fps.description: Videos: frames per second, when known.

has_audio.description: Whether a video carries an audio track (PixelGenie L10).

index.description: Position in the list; the `{index}` that streams this file.

kept.description:
`false` when litegen kept no copy (`keep_outputs: false`,
docs/storage-access.md): the file is the vendor's, and the vendor
deletes it on its own schedule. Absent when litegen kept it.

kind.description:
`image`, `video`, `mesh`, `texture`, `preview`, `original` or
`package`. A plain string so a client tolerates a kind added later.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored file.

url.description:
Where the file is served from: absolute; litegen's own storage, or the
vendor's link when `kept` is false.

ImageBackground.description: An image's background (PixelGenie L9): `transparent` is a real alpha channel.

ImageGenerationAccepted.description:
The answer to an image request that won't wait for its job
(`Prefer: respond-async`, or a `wait` the job outlasted): litegen
delivers the image to the generation when the vendor finishes
(docs/async-images.md).

id.description: The generation: `GET /v1/generations/{id}` serves its image once done.

oneOf.description:
`transparent` for a real alpha channel where the model supports it
(`supports_transparent_background`); needs `png` or `webp`.

directions.description: A character in 4 or 8 facings, one labelled image each (PixelGenie L16).

oneOf.description:
Grow the init image's canvas by this many pixels a side (3D doc §4);
the model's `expand` spec says how much and whether it only centres.

feather_px.description:
With `preserve_unmasked`: blend from the init at the edit area's edge
to the vendor's pixels this many pixels inside it (0, a hard edge, by
default; at most 256).

layout.description:
Boxes for a text-to-image canvas (3D doc §4): objects and words
placed by fractions of the canvas.

mask_grow_px.description:
Grow the edit area outward by this many pixels: the vendor's own
setting where it has one (sent explicitly, even as 0), else litegen
dilates the mask itself. Default 0.

mask_prompt.description:
The area an edit replaces, named in text rather than drawn as a mask
(3D doc §4).

oneOf.description:
The image container to return (PixelGenie L9): one of the model's
`capabilities.output_formats`. Omitted means the vendor's default.

palette.description:
Colours as `#rrggbb` (PixelGenie L16): every pixel one of them on a
model whose palette is forced, a hint elsewhere.

preserve_unmasked.description:
Paste the init image's pixels back outside the edit area (3D doc §4),
so they come back byte-identical from any vendor. Needs a mask or a
region, a lossless container and an output the init's size.

oneOf.description:
Edit only this rectangle of the `init` image (3D doc §4). A box-native
model receives it as its own box; a mask-only one receives it drawn as
the mask. With a `mask` too, the edit area is where they overlap.

resolution.description:
The output tier, on a model that has tiers: one of its
`params.resolution` values, on one scale for every vendor (`0.5K`,
`0.75K`, `1K`, `1.5K`, `2K`, `4K`, about that many thousand pixels a
side; FLUX 3 Image adds `match_input`, an edit at its reference's
size). An exact `size` wins where a model takes both.

views.description:
The views a `multiview` model makes, one image each, in this order.
Omitted means the model's default set.

ImageGenerationResponse.description:
Response for an image generation request.
Follows OpenAI's images response format for compatibility.

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the request was created.

provider.description: The provider that handled the request.

oneOf.description: Cost information.

ImageOutputFormat.description: An image container litegen asks a vendor for (PixelGenie L9).

ImageResult.description: A single generated image in the response.

direction.description:
The facing this image shows, from a `directions` request: `south`
(towards the viewer), `south-east`, `east`, … (PixelGenie L16).

expires_at.description:
When a signed link stops working (`docs/storage-access.md`); read the
generation again for a fresh one. Absent on every other URL.

revised_prompt.description: Revised prompt (if provider modified the prompt, e.g. DALL-E 3).

url.description: URL of the generated image (if response_format=url).

oneOf.description: The view this image shows, from a `multiview` model.

width.description: The image's size in pixels, read from its bytes.

yaw_deg.description: The camera's yaw for `view`, in degrees (see `ImageView`).

image.description: The image: base64, or a `data:` URI. PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF.

metadata.description: Your own labels for the call, as on a generation (L17).

prompts.description:
What to select. Point and box prompts together select one object;
a text prompt selects every instance of what it names.

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the request was created.

masks.description:
One per object selected, best score first. Empty when nothing was
found.

ImageView.description:
A side of the subject a view shows (3D doc §3E). Its `yaw_deg` is the
camera's position around +Y, measured from the subject's front (+Z)
towards +X — and glTF puts the subject's left at +X — so `front` is 0,
`left` 90, `back` 180 and `right` 270. `top` and `bottom` have no yaw.

InPlaceMode.description: Who keeps a clip in place.

org_id.description:
Organization the invitee will join on accept. Defaults to the
single-tenant default org for legacy/global invites.

role.description: The role the invited user will receive in `org_id` upon accepting.

KeyframeTiming.description: Where a model's keyframes may sit in the clip.

LatencyPercentiles.description: Latency percentiles for the last N minutes.

LayoutBox.description:
Where a layout box sits, as fractions of the canvas (0 to 1, top-left
origin): the output's size may not be known yet.

LayoutItem.description:
One box of a text-to-image layout (3D doc §4). Boxes guide the layout;
no vendor clips to them.

prompt.description: What goes there: required for an `object` box.

text.description: The words to render: required for a `text` box.

LayoutKind.description: What a layout box holds (3D doc §4).

LimitsInput.description:
Request body for `PUT …/limits`. A full replacement of the configurable
fields: an omitted field is cleared. Accumulated spend is kept unless the
budget window changes, which starts a fresh window from now.

LinksRevoked.description:
What a revocation answers: litegen's links issued before `revoked_at` no
longer work. A bucket's own presigned links aren't litegen's: they work
until they expire.

MaskConvention.description: Which pixels of a mask mean "edit".

McpEndpoints.description: The MCP endpoints a deployment serves, for the dashboard's Connect page.

admin_url.description: The management endpoint, `{public_base_url}/admin/mcp`, when it is served.

oauth.description: Whether clients can sign in with OAuth (ChatGPT and claude.ai need it).

Model3dAnimationPreset.description:
The canonical animation presets (`animations[].preset`, 3D doc §3C). A
model maps the ones it plays onto its own preset ids; a request may name
either.

Model3dAsset.description:
One file produced by a 3D generation, re-hosted on litegen storage (the
app's own bucket when it configured one).

A `completed` generation carries one `mesh` asset for every format in its
`output_formats` — never fewer; a missing one fails the generation instead —
plus whatever textures and previews the vendor returned, and, when the
request set `output_packages`, a `package` asset (a zip) for each of those
formats that is a file and its sidecars, after every other asset.

expires_at.description:
When a signed link stops working (`docs/storage-access.md`); read the
generation again for a fresh one. Absent on every other URL.

format.description:
Lowercase container without a dot. Meshes use the `Model3dFormat`
vocabulary; textures and previews their image format (`png`, `jpg`,
`webp`). A plain string so a client tolerates a format added later.

height.description: Pixel height, on textures and previews whose vendor reports it.

kept.description:
`false` when litegen kept no copy (`keep_outputs: false`): the file is
the vendor's own, unconverted, and the vendor deletes it on its own
schedule. Absent when litegen kept it.

polycount.description:
Triangle count, on meshes whose vendor reports one. A container litegen
derived carries its source's count — conversion keeps every triangle.

oneOf.description:
On meshes and packages: what litegen's own reader found in this very
file (a package's container read with its sidecars). Never the
vendor's claims.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored file.

url.description:
Always absolute: a root-relative path is indistinguishable from an
outage to a client fetching it from a worker. Meshes live at
`…/{generation_id}/model.{format}`, packages at
`…/{generation_id}/package_{format}.zip`.

width.description: Pixel width, on textures and previews whose vendor reports it.

Model3dConvertFormats.description: What the converter can do, for a client to check before uploading.

formats.description:
Containers accepted as both `from` and `to`. Every pair converts, in
both directions. Today every `Model3dFormat`; it follows litegen's
converter, so read it rather than hardcoding it.

max_input_bytes.description: Largest request body accepted, in bytes. Larger bodies get `413`.

Model3dDaeMorphs.description:
How a Collada (`dae`) file litegen writes stores a mesh's morph targets
(`dae_morphs`). Collada's morph controllers are read by only some tools, so
the caller chooses.

Model3dFbxColorSpace.description:
How a delivered or read FBX stores its material and light colours
(`fbx_color_space`). FBX does not say, and the tools that read it disagree.

Model3dFormat.description:
Every mesh container a 3D request may name in `output_formats`.

The closed vocabulary across all of litegen's 3D models. Which subset one
model can deliver is per model: `GET /v1/models/{id}` lists it under
`params.output_formats.enum_values`, and anything outside it is refused
with `param_enum_mismatch` before any vendor is called.

A container reaches a caller one of two ways. Either litegen derives it
locally from whatever readable container the vendor emitted — the set
`proxy::model3d_convert::derivable_formats` returns, served per model as
`params.output_formats.derivable_values` — and any number of those cost one
vendor job together; or the vendor emits it itself, one job each. Which is
which grows with `litegen-core/src/mesh/`, so this list is deliberately a
superset of every container any vendor or the converter produces.

Requests carry these as plain, case-insensitive strings — validation, not
deserialisation, owns the error, so it can name what IS deliverable. This
type pins the vocabulary for OpenAPI and for the catalog loader.

Model3dFormatSource.description: Where a delivered `fbx` or `usdz` comes from (`format_source`).

animations.description:
The clips to make, in order: one glTF animation per entry, named
exactly its `name`.

center.description:
Centre the mesh's bounds on x and z (3D doc §3D). litegen applies it
on delivery, to any model's mesh.

oneOf.description:
How the Collada (`dae`) litegen writes stores a mesh's morph targets,
when litegen writes one for this request (a vendor Collada delivered as
it is keeps the vendor's): `bake` (the default) applies the targets at
each node's weights and drops their weight animation, which every
Collada reader opens; `keep` writes them as `<morph>` controllers with
their weight animation, which SceneKit (and so Xcode) and Godot read,
while three.js's ColladaLoader and assimp refuse the whole file. A
request that keeps nothing (`keep_outputs: false`) can't ask for `keep`:
`option_needs_keeping`.

How FBX material and light colours are stored, when litegen reads the
vendor's FBX or writes one for this request (a vendor FBX delivered as
it is keeps the vendor's): `srgb` (the default; three.js reads them so)
or `linear` (Blender, ufbx and assimp read both so, and Unity and Unreal
material colours). Vertex colours are sRGB either way.

The units FBX light strengths are stored in, when litegen reads the
vendor's FBX or writes one for this request (a vendor FBX delivered as
it is keeps the vendor's units): `photometric` (the default; the
scene's own, as three.js's FBXLoader and ufbx read them: `Intensity` is
100 × the candela or lux) or `blender` (100 × the `energy` Blender's
own glTF importer gives the same scene's glTF light, so the lights open
in Blender as bright as the glTF does, and a vendor FBX that Blender
wrote reads as the glTF light whose import gives that `energy`).
Colours are in `fbx_color_space` either way.

Where a promised `fbx` or `usdz` comes from: `native` (the default)
asks the vendor for its own export when it offers one, and litegen
makes the other containers from that file; `glb` asks for the vendor's
GLB, which carries the most, and litegen makes them all from it. Either
way one vendor job is billed.

fps.description: Frames per second of the delivered clips.

ground.description:
Put the mesh's lowest point at y = 0 (3D doc §3D). litegen applies it
on delivery, to any model's mesh.

height_m.description:
The delivered mesh's height in metres (3D doc §3D): litegen scales
any mesh it delivers to it, and a rig model whose vendor takes a
height gets it too. At most 10,000 m, or within a model's own
`height_m` range.

oneOf.description:
The joint names to deliver the rig with. `vendor` (the default) keeps
the vendor's own.

keep_uvs.description: Paint the source's own UV layout rather than a new one.

oneOf.description:
What delivery does with a KTX2 (Basis Universal) texture, such as the
images of a GLB that requires `KHR_texture_basisu`. `png` (the default)
re-encodes it as PNG in every container, as WebP is, so no delivered
file needs an extension to read; the vendor's own file is delivered
beside it as `original`. `keep` leaves it as the vendor made it in the
`glb` and `gltf` containers (byte for byte, through
`KHR_texture_basisu`, which those files then require: for viewers that
upload KTX2 to the GPU, such as three.js with KTX2Loader, Babylon.js
and Godot), and every other container still gets PNG. A request that
keeps nothing (`keep_outputs: false`) can't ask for `keep`:
`option_needs_keeping`. litegen applies it on delivery, to any model's
mesh.

output_format.description: Superseded by `output_formats`. A lone value is folded into it; when both are sent, `output_formats` wins and this one is reported dropped.

output_formats.description:
Mesh containers to deliver, e.g. `["glb", "fbx"]`. A promise, not a
hint: every format named here is present on a `completed` generation,
or the generation ends `failed`. Omitted means the model's declared
default, and `["glb"]` when it declares none. Case-insensitive;
duplicates collapse.

Any set of the containers litegen derives (the model's served
`derivable_values`) costs one vendor job between them; every other
container costs one job of its own. A request needing more vendor jobs
than the model's `max_items` is refused with `param_too_many`.

output_packages.description:
Also deliver each requested container that is a file and its
sidecars (an `obj` with its `.mtl` and textures, a `dae`, `usda` or
`usdc` with its textures, a `gltf` with its `.bin` and images) as one zip of
them: an asset of kind `package` whose `format` is the container
inside. litegen applies it on delivery, to any model's mesh, and the
`mesh` assets stay as they are. A container that is one file for this
mesh gets no package. A request that keeps nothing (`keep_outputs:
false`) can't ask for packages: `option_needs_keeping`.

pbr.description: PBR materials. `false` asks for flat shading, not "no material".

rig.description: Auto-rig: deliver the mesh with a skeleton.

oneOf.description: The skeleton to rig for, from the model's `skeleton` enum.

The mesh an operation (`rig`, `animate`, `texture`, `remesh`,
`segment`) works on, required by every model whose task is not
`generate`. A litegen generation id chains a step onto the last; a URL
or base64 bytes bring a mesh of your own and name its `format`.
Symmetry handling.

target_polycount.description:
Approximate triangle budget for the mesh, within the model's declared
`target_polycount` range.

texture.description: Texture the mesh, rather than returning bare geometry.

texture_resolution.description:
A `texture` model's map size in pixels, one of its
`texture_resolutions`.

oneOf.description: Face topology of the output mesh.

Which animation clips the `usda`, `usdc` or `usdz` litegen writes for
this request holds (a vendor USD delivered as it is keeps the vendor's):
`all` keeps every clip as an alternative (a SkelAnimation prim for
each, chosen by a variant set `Animation`, as Apple's own tooling lays
them out), `first` keeps the first and names the rest in the losses.
Under `all` every clip's skeletal and blend-shape animation is kept;
rigid (node) motion is the first clip's only, the other clips' is
named in the losses, and a scene whose clips are all rigid writes as
`first`.
Unset is the container's default: `all` for `usda` and `usdc`, `first`
for `usdz` until AR Quick Look's behaviour with variants is checked on
a device. A request that keeps nothing (`keep_outputs: false`) can't
ask for `all`: `option_needs_keeping`.

The units USD light strengths are stored in, when litegen reads the
vendor's `usdz`, `usda` or `usdc` or writes one for this request (one delivered
as it is keeps the vendor's units): `photometric` (the default;
UsdLux's own, by the schema) or `blender` (the UsdLux values Blender's
USD exporter writes for the `energy` Blender's own
glTF importer gives the same scene's glTF light, so the lights open in
Blender as bright as the glTF does, and a vendor USD that Blender wrote
reads as the glTF light whose import gives that `energy`). A file
litegen wrote keeps its exact strengths in `customData`, which wins on
read under either choice.

What the root layer of a `usdz` litegen writes for this request is (a
vendor USDZ delivered as it is keeps the vendor's): `usda` (the
default) is text, which `usdchecker --arkit` accepts and which
`<model-viewer>` hands to AR Quick Look; `usdc` is the binary crate,
as Apple's own packagers write it. Either way the root is the
package's first entry, 64-byte aligned. A request that keeps nothing
(`keep_outputs: false`) can't ask for `usdc`: `option_needs_keeping`.

Model3dGenerationRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/models3d/generations` and `POST /v1/models3d/cost`.

The mode is inferred, never passed: no `reference_images` is text-to-3D, an
`init` image is image-to-3D, and `view-*` images are multiview-to-3D.

Every 3D param is optional and model-dependent; `GET /v1/models/{id}` →
`params` says which a model takes. One it does not take is refused with
`param_unsupported` when `strict` is true (the default), and dropped — and
named in the `X-Litegen-Dropped-Params` response header — when `strict` is
false. A supported param with a bad VALUE is refused in both modes.

Model3dGenerationResponse.description:
A 3D generation's state — both the submit response and every poll
response, since 3D generation is always async. Mirrors
`VideoGenerationResponse`, with `video_url` replaced by `assets`.

assets.description:
Populated on `completed`; omitted while in flight and on `failed`, so a
failed generation never looks half-usable.

created.description: Unix seconds when the generation was submitted.

error.description:
Why the generation failed, when it did. Vendor failures carry the
vendor's message, with its machine-readable type in parentheses when it
sent one.

id.description:
`litegen-3d-…`. Poll it at `GET /v1/models3d/{id}`; it is also the
generation's id under `/v1/generations`.

progress.description: 0–100. Vendors that only report queue state (fal) move in coarse steps.

oneOf.description:
The cost charged: quoted at submit, and 0 once a failed or cancelled
generation has been refunded (L18).

Model3dJointNaming.description: The joint names a rig is delivered with (`joint_naming`, 3D doc §3B).

Model3dKtx2Textures.description:
What delivery does with a KTX2 (Basis Universal) texture
(`ktx2_textures`).

Model3dLightUnits.description:
How a delivered or read FBX or USD stores its light strengths
(`fbx_light_units`, `usd_light_units`). Neither format says which units it
uses, and Blender reads them in its own units rather than glTF's
photometric ones.

Model3dSkeleton.description:
The skeleton a rig is built for (`skeleton`, 3D doc §3B): Tripo's
`rig_type` values, with its `biped` named `humanoid`.

Model3dSymmetry.description: Symmetry handling a 3D request may ask for (`symmetry`).

Model3dTopology.description: Face topology a 3D request may ask for (`topology`).

Model3dUsdClips.description:
Which animation clips a USD file litegen writes holds (`usd_clips`). USD has
one timeline, so a scene with several clips keeps them as alternatives or
keeps the first.

Model3dUsdzRoot.description:
What the root layer of a `usdz` litegen writes is (`usdz_root`). Both pass
`usdchecker --arkit`, and every USD reader opens either, so the caller
chooses.

directions.description: The `directions` counts it takes; empty when none.

duration_values.description:
The only `duration_seconds` values the model takes; empty when it
takes its range.

oneOf.description: An `extend` model's answer: the whole clip or only the added part.

`any`: each keyframe at its own time; `even`: evenly spaced over the
clip, start and end included.

layout_kinds.description: What its layout boxes may hold; empty when it takes no layout.

oneOf.description:
The mask convention a caller sends: `white_edits` on every model that
takes a mask, whatever its vendor reads — litegen converts.

max_duration_seconds.description: The longest clip the model makes, from its `duration_seconds` param.

max_keyframes.description: The most `keyframe` references one request may carry.

max_polycount.description: Upper bound of the model's `target_polycount` param, when it takes one.

max_reference_images.description:
The most reference images one request may carry. Kept under its old
name too: `max_images` is this same number (L14).

output_formats.description:
Every mesh container a caller may request, including those litegen
derives locally — the same list, in the same order, as
`GET /v1/models/{id}` serves under `params.output_formats.enum_values`.
Empty for image and video models.

oneOf.description: A native pixel-art model's output edge, in pixels.

What the vendor promises about pixels outside the edit, in its own
words: `exact`, `similar` or `unspecified`.

How the model receives a `region`: `box` (its own box) or `mask`
(drawn as its mask).

segmentation_prompts.description:
The prompt types it segments by: `point`, `box`, `text`. Empty when it
does not segment.

supports_animation.description:
Takes `animations`: one clip per entry, whatever the task (3D doc
§3C) — a rig or generate model that returns clips in the same call
as well as an `animate` one.

supports_audio_toggle.description: Takes `audio: false` (or `true`) to leave audio out (or in).

supports_background_removal.description:
Takes one `init` image and returns it as an RGBA PNG with its
background removed (PixelGenie L8).

supports_forced_palette.description: Every pixel of its output is one of the palette's colours.

supports_keyframes.description: Takes `keyframe` references, each pinned at its `time_s` (3D doc §5).

supports_mask_grow.description:
Takes `mask_grow_px`: litegen widens the mask or region of any model
taking one, or asks a vendor that grows its own (3D doc §4).

supports_palette.description: Takes `palette`, as a hint or forced.

supports_placement.description:
Takes `ground`, `center` and `height_m`, which litegen applies to every
mesh it delivers: true on every 3D model.

supports_preserve_unmasked.description:
Takes `preserve_unmasked`, which litegen applies to any model taking a
mask or a region (3D doc §4).

supports_skeleton.description:
Takes `skeleton`; `params.skeleton.enum_values` lists what it rigs
(3D doc §3B).

supports_source_model.description: Takes `source_model`: an operation on an existing mesh.

supports_text_to_3d.description: Accepts a prompt with no reference images (text-to-3D).

task.description:
What the model does: `generate`, or an operation on an existing asset
such as `rig` or `animate`. The same value `GET /v1/models/{id}`
serves as `task`. Always sent.

texture_resolutions.description:
The map sizes a `texture` model paints at (`texture_resolution`);
empty when it takes none.

background_removal.description:
Takes one `init` image and returns it as an RGBA PNG with the
background made transparent (PixelGenie L8).

native_pixel_art.description:
Draws native pixel art: its output is at native size, one image pixel
per art pixel, and needs no reducing (PixelGenie L16).

is_available.description: Whether the model's provider can serve this caller (L14).

oneOf.description: Pricing information.

replaced_by.description: The catalog model to move to.

retires_at.description:
The vendor's shutdown date (`YYYY-MM-DD`): litegen stops serving it the
day after.

status.description: Where the model is in its vendor's lifecycle (L14).

catalog_version.description: Changes whenever any served model's field does (L14).

base_cost_usd.description: Base cost per image/video in USD.

variable_pricing.description:
How the price follows the request: ordered rules over a running
price that starts at `base_cost_usd` (see `PriceRule`).

ModelRoute.description: Routing configuration for a model, with fallbacks and weights.

oneOf.description: Cache settings for this model.

area, in its own words.

The vendor's announced shutdown date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). From the day

task.description:
What the model does: `generate`, or an operation on an existing asset
such as `rig` or `animate`. A row or a runtime model may leave it out

ModelSource.description: Where a served model definition comes from.

ModelTask.description:
What a catalog model does.

An operation on an existing asset is a model of its own, submitted to its
modality's one job endpoint: `tripo/rig` and `meshy/animate` go to
`POST /v1/models3d/generations` like any generation, and are polled,
priced, cancelled, re-hosted and billed the same way, because each
produces a new asset.

One task per model. `generate` is the default in every modality. It still
covers image edits driven by `init` and `mask` references, and 3D models
that infer text, image or multiview input from their references.

NativeOrientation.description:
The axes a 3D model's vendor builds its meshes along (3D doc §2 rule 3).
Where they differ from glTF's (+Y up, +Z front), litegen adds a root
rotation and the manifest says `oriented_by: "litegen"`. An operation that
hands back its source's own geometry says `source` for both: its output
faces wherever the source did.

evidence.description: What showed it: the run, sample file or page.

front.description:
The axis the asset's front faces, at right angles to `up`; `source`
with `up`.

up.description:
`+x`, `-x`, `+y`, `-y`, `+z` or `-z`; `source` on an operation that
keeps its source's axes.

max_items.description: The most boxes one request may send.

single_word_text.description: Each text box holds one word (Recraft's `text_layout`).

ParamSpecPalette.description: `palette` on an image model (PixelGenie L16): the colours it keeps to.

forced.description:
Every pixel is one of the palette's colours (PixelLab's forced
palette, Retro Diffusion's `input_palette`); otherwise the palette is
a hint (Ideogram's `color_palette`, Recraft's `controls`).

max_colors.description: The most colours one palette may hold.

ParamSpecSegmentationPrompts.description:
`prompts` on a segmentation model (PixelGenie L7): what it can be asked
to select.

max_items.description: The most prompts one request may send.

max_masks.description:
The most masks one answer holds: a text prompt finds at most this
many instances.

types.description: The prompt types the model takes, listed as `segmentation_prompts`.

ParamSpecSourceModel.description:
What an operation on an existing mesh takes as its `source_model` (3D doc
§3A). litegen reads the source with its own mesh reader and refuses one the
vendor would refuse — before the billed submit — then converts it to a
container in `formats` if it is not already one.

formats.description:
Containers the vendor accepts, from the `Model3dFormat` vocabulary. A
source in any other container litegen can read is converted to the
first of these it can write.

max_bytes.description: Largest file the vendor accepts, in bytes, as sent.

requires_skin.description: The source must already be rigged (have a skin).

ParamSpecSourceVideo.description: `source_video` on a video operation (3D doc §5): the clips it works on.

oneOf.description: An `extend` model's answer: the whole clip, or only the added part.

max_duration_s.description: The longest source it takes, in seconds.

own_generations_only.description:
Only the vendor's own earlier generations, on the same account (Luma,
Kling): any other source is `source_not_chainable`.

ParamSpecStringArray.description:
A param whose value is a SET of enum members rather than one of them.

Exists for `output_formats`, where the vendors genuinely disagree on
cardinality: Meshy emits every requested container from one job, Rodin's
`geometry_file_format` is a scalar so only one is reachable, and Stability
emits GLB with no choice at all. `max_items` is how a model states which of
those it is, so an unsatisfiable request fails in validation rather than
after the vendor has been billed.

For `output_formats` the catalog yaml and the API describe two different
sets, on purpose:

- **yaml** `enum_values` declares what the VENDOR emits natively — the only
  thing a catalog author can verify against the vendor's schema.
- **`GET /v1/models/{id}`** serves what a CALLER may request: the native
  set plus every container litegen derives locally, with `derivable_values`
  saying which those are. That is the same set the validator accepts, so a
  client rendering `params` offers exactly what will be honoured.

default.description:
Applied when the caller omits the param entirely. Empty means the
resolver falls back to `glb`.

derivable_values.description:
The members litegen produces locally from a single vendor job (for
`output_formats`, whatever its mesh converter covers — today `glb`,
`obj`, `stl`, `ply`). Present only in API
responses, and only when the model's vendor emits at least one of them —
with nothing readable to convert from, nothing is derivable. Computed
by the server; the catalog loader refuses a yaml that sets it.

enum_values.description:
Accepted members. See the type docs for what this means in yaml versus
in an API response.

max_items.description:
For `output_formats`: how many VENDOR jobs one request may need — not
how many members it may name. Every member of `derivable_values` comes
out of one source container, so a request costs
`|requested \ derivable_values| + (requested ∩ derivable_values ≠ ∅ ? 1 : 0)`
jobs, and more than `max_items` is refused with `param_too_many`.
`None` means no limit.

ParamSpecTimeRange.description: `time_range` on a video operation (3D doc §5): the windows it takes.

min_window_s.description: The shortest window, in seconds (LTX's 2 s).

whole_seconds.description: Starts and ends fall on whole seconds (Runway).

PixelSize.description: The smallest and largest output edge, in pixels (PixelGenie L16).

PreservesUnmasked.description: What a vendor promises about the pixels outside an edit.

PriceRule.description:
One pricing rule. When every `when` entry matches the request, its one
effect applies: a price (`usd`), a rate (`per_second_usd` × the clip's
seconds, `per_megapixel_usd` × the image's megapixels, `per_item_usd` × the
count of the `per_item` list) or an adjustment (`multiply`, `add_usd`).

multiply_per_megapixel_above.description:
Scale the price by the image's `megapixels` over this many, for an
image larger than this: a vendor that bills by output size (OpenAI's
image tokens) past the size its base price is for.

when.description:
Request facts the rule needs: a param (as sent, else its default), an
`extra.<field>`, or a derived fact (the `views`, `added_views`,
`keyframes`, `animations` and `references` counts, `duration_seconds`,
`megapixels`), each mapped to the value it must have, `"*"` for any
value present, or a range a number must fall in, such as
`{"gt": 1.048576, "lte": 4.194304}` (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`).

PromptSpec.description: How a model treats the request's `prompt`. Lengths count characters.

max_length.description:
`0` means the model takes no prompt at all (an image-only endpoint
whose vendor has no prompt field): a client should not offer one, and a
non-empty prompt is refused in strict mode and dropped in lax mode.

required.description:
An empty or omitted prompt is refused with `prompt_required`. 3D models
that take images set this false, yet still need a prompt when a request
carries no image (text-to-3D).

ProviderCatalogEntry.description:
Describes a provider and how the dashboard should render its credential
form. Returned by `GET /v1/providers` so the UI never hard-codes per-provider
field knowledge.

fields.description: Fields to collect per pool entry, besides the universal `weight`/`label`.

modalities.description: Which media this provider serves — any of "image", "video".

pool_field.description:
Which credentials array to submit: "api_keys" (bearer) or
"credential_sets" (signing). Each array element is `{<fields…>, weight?, label?}`.

enabled.description: Whether this provider config is enabled.

model_mapping.description: Model ID mapping: internal ID → provider's model ID.

ProviderConfigView.description: Admin view of one provider: what is configured, with every secret masked.

active.description: Whether a live instance is registered and serving requests.

extra_header_names.description: Header names only; values can carry secrets.

key_hint.description: Last 4 characters of the effective key, e.g. `…a1b2`. Never the secret.

modalities.description: Media this adapter can serve: image, video, model3d.

source.description: Where the effective config comes from: `env`, `runtime` or `none`.

ProviderCredentialInfo.description: Public view of a stored BYO provider credential — NEVER the plaintext secret.

ProviderSettings.description:
Non-secret part of a runtime provider config. Unset fields fall back to the
provider's env/YAML config.

enabled.description: False takes the provider out of service until re-enabled.

PublicUser.description: Public user view returned from user management endpoints.

PutAppAccessRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/apps/{app_id}/access`: the app's settings, every one replaced.
An omitted or `null` field uses the gateway's value; `{}` clears them all.

keep_outputs.description:
`false` keeps nothing: answers carry the vendor's own link, or the
image itself.

oneOf.description: `public`, `signed` or `private`.
`key`, `app` or `org`.

retention_days.description: 0 to 36500; 0 keeps files until they are deleted.

oneOf.description: `store` or `litegen`.

access_key_id.description: Write-only. Provide WITH `secret_access_key` to set/rotate; omit BOTH to keep existing.

credential_mode.description:
`access_key` (default: the key pair above) or `assume_role` (a
cross-account IAM role, `role_arn`, trusting litegen with the app's
`external_id`).

fallback_to_litegen_store.description:
Whether litegen's own store keeps the app's files while its bucket
can't be reached (default true). With false, they wait for the bucket.

PutProviderConfigRequest.description:
Request body for `PUT /v1/admin/providers/{name}`. Secret fields left out
keep their stored (or env) value, so an api_base change needs no key.

data_uri.description:
Whether the vendor takes a `data:` URI where it takes a URL (default
yes). When it does not, litegen publishes an uploaded reference at an
unguessable URL of its own for the vendor to fetch (L4).

view_order.description:
For a multiview-to-3D vendor that takes its views as ONE ordered list
(3D doc §3E): the views in that list's order. A view needs every view
before it, since the vendor reads them by position. Empty when the
vendor takes each view by name and any may be omitted.

oneOf.description:
The mask role's VENDOR convention: which pixels it edits. Callers
always send white-edits masks; litegen converts.

max_time_s.description:
The latest a `keyframe` may sit, for a model with no duration param
to bound its clip: the longest clip it makes or prices.

native_grow.description:
The mask role's vendor grows masks itself (Stability's `grow_mask`):
`mask_grow_px` goes to it, explicitly, instead of litegen dilating.

time_step_s.description:
The `keyframe` role's time grid, when the vendor takes only multiples
of it (PixVerse: whole seconds). A time off it is refused.

oneOf.description:
The `keyframe` role's timing (3D doc §5): `any` time each, or `even`
spacing over the clip. Required on that role, refused on others.

time_s.description:
Seconds from the start of the clip, on a `keyframe` reference (3D doc
§5): the video shows this image at that time.

Region.description:
A rectangle of an image, in its pixels: top-left origin, ends exclusive
(it covers `x..x+w` by `y..y+h`). Named keys, never arrays: vendors
disagree on axis order.

RequestArtifact.description: Stores the input/output snapshot of a generation request for drill-down.

RevokeKeyResponse.description: Response for `DELETE /v1/keys/{id}` and similar revocation endpoints.

RotatedKeyResponse.description:
Response for `POST /v1/keys/{id}/rotate`. Carries the freshly-minted secret,
which is returned exactly once (it is never persisted or shown again).

key.description: The new secret, e.g. "sk_live_…". Shown only at rotation time.

scopes.description: CSV of scopes carried over from the rotated key.

RouteDeployment.description: One provider a route can dispatch to.

RouteSpec.description: A model route: which providers serve models matching `model`, and how.

source.description: `config` while the routes come from litegen.yaml, `runtime` once replaced through the API.

in_place.description: Measured: the root ends within 1 cm of where it started, horizontally.

in_place_by.description:
`vendor` (arrived in place), `litegen` (litegen removed the root's
horizontal travel), or absent when not in place.

loop_requested.description: Whether the request asked for a loop (a hint; glTF has no loop flag).

root_travel_m.description: The root's world displacement, first key to last, in metres.

SceneManifest.description:
What litegen measured in a delivered mesh (3D doc §3D). Every delivered
mesh is in glTF's conventions: metres, +Y up, the subject facing +Z with
its right side at −X.

oneOf.description: World-space bounds at rest, in metres.

extensions_used.description: glTF extensions the file uses (none is ever required).

front.description:
`+z`, or `unverified` when the model's orientation has not been proven
(litegen never reports a guess).

notes.description:
What delivery could not keep or do for this file: a texture litegen
could not decode, a joint naming the rig could not take, what this
container cannot hold of the scene. Empty when nothing was lost.

parts.description:
A `segment` model's parts: one glTF node each, named with the
vendor's label or `part_<n>`. Absent on every other model's mesh.

ScenePart.description: One part of a segmented mesh, measured by litegen.

oneOf.description: World-space bounds at rest, in metres.

node.description: The part's node: its index in the delivered glTF's `nodes`.

bind_pose.description: `t`, `a` or `unknown`, from the upper-arm angle at rest.

humanoid.description:
VRM 1.0 humanoid bone → joint name, for a rig litegen recognises;
`null` for one it does not (never a guess).

joints.description: Joint names, unique, in skin order.

skeleton.description:
`humanoid` when a known naming scheme matched, else what the request
asked the rig to be, else absent.

SegmentOrigin.description: Where a stretch of a finished clip came from (3D doc §5).

box.description: The smallest box around the white pixels, measured by litegen.

png_base64.description:
A grayscale PNG the size of the image: white (255) where selected,
black (0) elsewhere.

score.description: The vendor's confidence, 0–1; null when it gives none.

oneOf.description:
A spot on the object (`label: 1`, the default) or one to leave out
of it (`label: 0`).
A box around the object; ends exclusive, as `Region`.
What to select, named.

SegmentationPrompt.description:
One thing to select, in the image's pixels (top-left origin). Point and
box prompts together select ONE object; a text prompt selects every
instance of what it names and cannot be mixed with them.

SegmentationPromptType.description: The kinds of segmentation prompt (PixelGenie L7).

SessionInfo.description:
Public session info. `id` is a NON-secret SHA-256 fingerprint of the session
token — never the raw token. The session row's primary key IS the bearer
credential (it's the `litegen_session` cookie value), so returning it
verbatim would let any response-body capture (e.g. XSS — which HttpOnly is
meant to stop) harvest usable session tokens for all the user's devices.
Revocation resolves the fingerprint back to the row.

id.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the session token (safe to expose; used for revoke).

org_name.description: Optional organization name (hosted mode). Defaults to the email local-part.

max_aspect.description: The widest long-to-short side ratio the vendor makes.

min_pixels.description:
The fewest and most pixels (width × height) the vendor makes (L13: a
size it cannot make is refused, never snapped).

SourceKind.description: How a `SourceRef`'s `value` is to be read.

SourceRef.description:
Where an operation's input comes from: a stored litegen generation, or a
file of your own.

oneOf.description:
The container, from the `Model3dFormat` vocabulary. Required for `url`
and `base64`; a generation's is known.

value.description:
The generation id, the URL, or the base64 bytes (a `data:` URI prefix
is allowed).

SpendGroupBy.description: Dimension a spend report is grouped by.

SpendLogEntry.description: One request in the spend log, with its attribution.

SpendReportRow.description: One group of a spend report.

group.description:
The group value (a day `YYYY-MM-DD`, model id, key id, …). Null when the
requests carried no value for the dimension (e.g. no end user).

TimeRange.description: A window of a clip, in seconds from its start (3D doc §5).

scopes.description:
Replace the key's scopes: the same values and the same privilege check
as on create (an unknown scope is a 400, one the caller may not grant a
403).

UpdateEndUserRequest.description: Request body for `PATCH /v1/end-users/{id}`. Omitted fields are unchanged.

UsageInfo.description: Cost / usage information for a generation.

cost_source.description: Cost source: "dynamic" (from API) or "estimated" (from pricing table).

VendorError.description:
What a vendor said when it refused or failed a request (PixelGenie L15):
its HTTP status (none when it never answered), its own error code and its
message.

VideoCamera.description: A video's camera (PixelGenie L10): `fixed` holds the shot still.

audio.description:
`false` for a silent clip, where the model can leave audio out
(`supports_audio_toggle`).

oneOf.description:
`fixed` for a still camera, where the model takes one
(`supports_fixed_camera`, PixelGenie L10).

direction.description: An `extend`: add before (`backward`) or after (`forward`) the source.

duration_seconds.description:
Absent means the model's own `duration_seconds` default (resolved by
`resolve_duration_seconds`), not a fixed 5s: models whose minimum is
higher (fal/ltx-2.3, bedrock nova-reel) rejected every request that
omitted it.

loop.description: `true` for a clip whose last frame is its first (`supports_loop`).

oneOf.description:
The clip an operation (`extend`, `retake`, `video_edit`) works on (3D
doc §5): a litegen generation id, a URL or base64, as `source_model`.
A `retake`'s window, or a `video_edit`'s where the model takes one.

VideoGenerationResponse.description: Video generation can be async — this is the initial response.

oneOf.description: What came back, read from the finished video (PixelGenie L10).

segments.description:
An operation's clip, stretch by stretch: from the source or generated
(3D doc §5). Absent on a plain generation.

oneOf.description: Cost information.

video_url_expires_at.description:
When `video_url` stops working, if it is a signed link
(`docs/storage-access.md`); poll again for a fresh one.

VideoMedia.description: What a finished video is, read from its bytes (PixelGenie L10).

VideoSegment.description: One stretch of a finished operation's clip, in its own seconds.
